test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 22 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Consider two wires of the same resistance, but the ratio of their cross-sectional areas is 1 ∶ 9. Furthermore, the ratio of their lengths is 3 ∶ 2. The ratio of their resistivities will be:
solution:
The correct answer is __**2 ∶ 27**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

**Resistance (R)** is given by the formula:

 R = (rho . l )/(A)R=ρ⋅LA" id="MathJax-Element-1-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">LA LA R = \frac{\rho \cdot L}{A}

Where, rho is the resistivity, l is the length, and A is the cross-sectional area.

Given that the resistances of the two wires are equal:

R₁ = R₂

(rho₁ . l₁)/(A₁) = (rho₂ . l₂)/(A₂)

From the problem,

(A₁)/(A₂) = (1)/(9)A1A2=19" id="MathJax-Element-6-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">A1A2=19" id="MathJax-Element-2-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">A1A2=19A1A2=19" id="MathJax-Element-31-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">A1A2=19A1A2=19 A1A2=19 A1A2=19 A1A2=19 \frac{A_1}{A_2} = \frac{1}{9} and (l₁)/(l₂) = (3)/(2)L1L2=32" id="MathJax-Element-7-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">L1L2=32" id="MathJax-Element-3-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">L1L2=32L1L2=32" id="MathJax-Element-32-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">L1L2=32L1L2=32 L1L2=32 L1L2=32 L1L2=32 

Substituting these values, we get:

(rho₁ . l₁)/(l₂) = (rho₂ . A₁)/(A₂)

(rho₁ . 3)/(2) = (rho₂ . 1)/(9)

Solving this, we get

(rho₁)/(rho₂) = (2)/(27)

Hence, the ratio of their resistivities is **2 ∶ 27**.
